paragraphs: Nani, son of Rav Yosef, son of Rava.
In Yevamot 66b, Nani challenges Rav Kahana: “But did not Rava say in the name of Rav Nachman,” etc.

notes.text: The frozen notice has ר״ב as the person challenged. The corresponding Yevamot66b paragraph names Rav Kahana. The abbreviation is not falsely expanded to Kahana; the mismatch remains for source review. The primary has Nanai, against the heading’s Nani form.

Hyman (vol. III, p. 918) prints לר״כ, where the supplied Hebrew has לר״ב. The consulted Yevamot 66b text explicitly names Rav Kahana as the person addressed and calls the speaker Nanai, son of Rav Yosef, son of Rava. It gives the same chain of attribution. Hyman’s heading has Nani.
